chunks: From him, from Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father and Muhammad ibn Isma'il, from al-Fadl ibn Shadhan, from Ibn Abi Umayr, from Abd al-Rahman ibn al-Hajjaj, from Abu al-Hasan (peace be upon him): Regarding

A man has the wealth of orphans with some of his family members, so he entrusts it to him. He takes from it dirhams that he needs, without informing the one holding the orphans' wealth that he took something from their money. Later, when he becomes able, which is better for him: to give it to the one who held it in his hand, or to deliver it to the orphan who has come of age? And is it sufficient for him to deliver it to the owner in the manner of a gift, without informing him that he took wealth for him? He (peace be upon him) said: 'It is sufficient for him whatever he does, as long as he conveys it to the owner, for this is from the secrets (khawas). If it is from his intention that if he wishes, he returns it to the orphan if he has come of age, in whatever manner he wishes, and if he did not inform him that he had taken something for him, and if he wishes, he returns it to the one who held it in his hand.' And he (peace be upon him) said: 'If the owner of the wealth is absent, let him deliver it to the one who had the wealth in his hand.'

key_terms.عَلَى وَجْهِ الصِّلَةِ: in the manner of a gift
key_terms.وَقَدْ بَلَغَ: and he has come of age
key_terms.يُدْفَعُ إِلَى الْيَتِيمِ: to be delivered to the orphan

ai.seo_question: What is the ruling if a trustee uses orphans' money without permission and later wants to repay it?
ai.summary: In this hadith from *Tahdhib al-Ahkam*, Imam al-Sadiq (AS) clarifies the ruling for a trustee who secretly consumes orphans' wealth, establishing that returning the equivalent value to either the now-adult orphan or the original custodian is sufficient. This flexibility highlights the concept of *khawas* (private discretion) in fiduciary duties, provided the intent is to settle the debt. The ruling emphasizes that the primary obligation is the restoration of value rather than strict procedural uniformity, reflecting the practical jurisprudence of managing minor's assets.
